paper.title: In-Context Reinforcement Learning through Bayesian Fusion of Context and Value Prior

settings.name_in_paper: stochastic A-armed bandit with sigma^2-sub-Gaussian rewards (SPICE inference with ensemble prior)
unmapped: learner is given a per-arm Gaussian prior (mean mu_pri_a, variance v_pri_a) from a pretrained value ensemble; the bound depends on the prior's miscalibration |mu_pri_a - mu_a|
settings.definition_quote: Consider a stochastic $A$-armed bandit setting with unknown means $\{\mu_a\}_{a=1}^A \subset \mathbb{R}$. At each round $t \in {1,...,K}$ the algorithm chooses $a_t$ and receives a reward $r_t = \mu_{a_t} + \varepsilon_t$, where $(\varepsilon_t)_{t \geq 1}$ are independent mean zero $\sigma-$sub-Gaussian noise variables. ... we scale rewards so that means satisfy $\mu_a \in [0.1]$

settings.name_in_paper: finite-horizon MDP (SPICE inference with ensemble Q prior)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Episodic finite-horizon MDP (reinforcement learning), not a bandit problem.
unmapped: finite state space of size S and action space of size A, episodes of length H
learner given per-(s,a) Gaussian prior from ensemble
settings.definition_quote: We consider a finite-horizon MDP $M = \langle \mathcal{S}, \mathcal{A}, P, R, H \rangle$ with finite state and action spaces $|\mathcal{S}| = S$, $|\mathcal{A}| = A$, transition kernel $P$, reward function $R$ bounded in $[0,1]$, and fixed episode length $H$. We run SPICE for $K$ episodes

algorithms.name: SPICE (posterior-UCB inference controller)
requires_knowledge_of: prior mean and variance per arm (from ensemble)

symbols.N_pri_i: prior pseudo-count sigma^2 / v_pri_i of arm i
symbols.mu_pri_i: prior mean of arm i from the value ensemble

source.label: theorem:regret_bound
source.quote: Under the assumption of $\sigma^2$-sub-Gaussian reward distributions, the SPICE inference controller satisfies \mathbb{E} [ \sum_{t=1}^K (\mu_\star - \mu_{a_t}) ] \leq \sum_{a \neq \star} ( \frac{32 \sigma^2 \log K}{\Delta_a^2}  + 4 N^{\text{pri}}_a |\mu_a^{\text{pri}} - \mu_a|) + O(1).

results.notes: Paper's K is the horizon T; A is the number of arms. Bound is explicit plus an additive O(1); recorded with notation O. The appendix restatement has Delta_a instead of Delta_a^2 in the log term (inconsistent); main-text version recorded. Horizon marked anytime since beta_t does not depend on K, though the proof fixes K.

conditions: ensemble prior perfectly calibrated: mu_pri_a = mu_a for all arms

source.quote: If the ensemble prior is perfectly calibrated, then $\mu_a^{\text{pri} } = \mu_a$ for all arms $a$ and the warm-start term vanishes. SPICE then reduces to classical UCB \mathbb{E}[R_K] \leq \sum_{a \neq \star} \frac{32\sigma^2\log K}{\Delta_a^2} + O(1).

results.notes: Special case of Theorem 1 with condition on the prior.

source.quote: If the ensemble prior has infinite variance, $v_a^{\text{pri}} \rightarrow \infty$ and therefore $N_A^{\text{pri}} \rightarrow 0  $. The warm-start term vanishes and SPICE reduces to classical UCB \autoref{eq:classic_ucb}.

conditions: Assumption 1: n-step TD targets unbiased for Q_star and conditionally sigma_Q-sub-Gaussian with sigma_Q^2 <= c_H H
tuning: beta_t = C_beta sqrt(log(S A T)), C_beta >= 2 sqrt(1+N_max)

source.label: theorem:mdp_regret
source.quote: Then the cumulative regret over $K$ episodes satisfies \mathbb{E}[\mathrm{Regret}_K] \le O(H\sqrt{SAK}) + \sum_{(s,a)\in\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}} O(N^{\mathrm{pri}}_{s,a}|\mu^{\mathrm{pri}}_{s,a} - Q_\star(s,a)|), where $\pi_k$ is the policy used in episode $k$ and the constants in the big-$O$ notation do not depend on $K$.

results.notes: Out-of-scope MDP result. Proof absorbs log factor (beta_T) into constant; the warm-start bound's constant in the proof is KH/N_pri, contradicting the claim of K-independence. Regret defined via value differences.
